ENGLISH LANGUAGE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #4
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Where would you find facts about elephants? (1 mark)
   A. A timetable
   B. A calendar
   C. A form
   D. A junior encyclopaedia

2. Which of these tells you what a book is about before you read it? (1 mark)
   A. The page numbers
   B. The printer's name
   C. The price sticker
   D. The back cover summary

3. What is a proverb? (1 mark)
   A. A long story
   B. A short well-known saying that gives advice or a truth
   C. A page of a dictionary
   D. A kind of song

4. The inbox is where (1 mark)
   A. the keyboard is stored
   B. deleted files are burnt
   C. messages you receive are kept
   D. messages waiting to be sent are kept

5. Which is the past participle of 'break'? (1 mark)
   A. breaked
   B. breaking
   C. broken
   D. broke

6. A visual is something we (1 mark)
   A. hear only
   B. taste
   C. smell
   D. understand by looking at it

7. What is a byline? (1 mark)
   A. A picture
   B. An advert
   C. The price of the paper
   D. The name of the writer of an article

8. Pronouns: Which sentence is correct? (1 mark)
   A. The house is our's.
   B. The house is ours's.
   C. The house is ours'.
   D. The house is ours.

9. Which is better for sharing a lot of news and feelings? (1 mark)
   A. A one-word SMS
   B. A letter
   C. A phone number
   D. A signature

10. What is the job of a full stop? (1 mark)
   A. To show a list
   B. To show a question
   C. To show strong feeling
   D. To end a statement or a command

11. 'Sleep like a log' means (1 mark)
   A. sleep very little
   B. sleep very deeply
   C. wake up early
   D. sleep in the forest

12. Which is the correct order for the parts of a narrative? (1 mark)
   A. End, beginning, middle
   B. Beginning, middle, end
   C. Middle, end, beginning
   D. End, middle, beginning

13. Which is a yes/no question? (1 mark)
   A. Where is the bin?
   B. What did you sweep?
   C. Who is the captain?
   D. Is the compound clean?

14. What does 'for' mean when it is used as a conjunction? (1 mark)
   A. because
   B. before
   C. however
   D. although

15. What is a stranger? (1 mark)
   A. A person you do not know
   B. Your teacher
   C. A person who lives next door
   D. A close friend

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Explain the difference between a factual and an inferential question and give an example of each from the story. (4 marks)

17. Say whether the voice falls or rises at the end of: (a) Who sent the message? (b) Is the phone on the table? (2 marks)

18. Give three strategies that help you read more fluently. (3 marks)

19. Write four sentences using north, south, east and west to describe the position of places near your school. (4 marks)

20. Punctuate: 'mama may i go to the shop' (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #4 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — A junior encyclopaedia
   An encyclopaedia gives facts about many subjects.

2. D — The back cover summary
   The back cover gives a short summary.

3. B — A short well-known saying that gives advice or a truth
   Proverbs teach lessons.

4. C — messages you receive are kept
   The outbox holds messages waiting to be sent.

5. C — broken
   Break, broke, broken.

6. D — understand by looking at it
   Pictures, signs, maps and videos are visuals.

7. D — The name of the writer of an article
   A byline says who wrote the article.

8. D — The house is ours.
   Possessive pronouns are written without an apostrophe.

9. B — A letter
   A letter can hold more news.

10. D — To end a statement or a command
   A full stop ends statements and commands.

11. B — sleep very deeply
   A log does not move, so it means a deep sleep.

12. B — Beginning, middle, end
   Stories move from beginning to end.

13. D — Is the compound clean?
   It starts with a helping verb and can be answered yes or no.

14. A — because
   'For' gives a reason.

15. A — A person you do not know
   A stranger is someone you do not know.

SECTION B
----
16. (4 marks)
   Answer: A factual question has its answer stated in the text: 'Where was Omondi's mother?' An inferential question needs clues: 'How did Omondi feel at the start?'
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 for each example.

17. (2 marks)
   Answer: (a) falls (b) rises
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

18. (3 marks)
   Answer: Preview the text; read in phrases; follow the punctuation; re-read; read along with a model.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

19. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: The gate is south of the classroom. The field is east of the gate. The library is west of the field. The road is north of the school.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence.

20. (2 marks)
   Answer: Mama, may I go to the shop?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for capitals and comma, 1 for the question mark.
